REGISTER: hpmcounter18
SUMMARY: hpmcounter18 is an unprivileged 64‑bit CSR that provides a read‑only view of the machine‑mode performance counter mhpmcounter18; it exists only if the Zihpm extension is implemented, otherwise it may be absent or return a constant and any access can raise an illegal‑instruction exception. mhpmcounter18 (one of mhpmcounter3–mhpmcounter31) is a 64‑bit event counter whose existence, width and counting capability are defined by the platform; after a hart reset its contents are undefined until software writes it (the write becomes visible after the instruction retires) and implementations may legally make it permanently zero. Access to hpmcounter18 is gated by enable bits: the HPM18 bit in mcounteren must be set for S‑mode accesses, and for U‑mode accesses both the HPM18 bits in mcounteren and scounteren must be set; if a required bit is clear the read raises an illegal‑instruction exception. When virtualization is active (V=1), the HPM18 bit in hcounteren also controls access: if it is clear a virtual‑instruction exception is raised in V‑mode (including VU‑mode), otherwise access follows the privilege‑mode enable rules. In M‑mode accesses never raise an exception regardless of extension presence, and any attempt to write hpmcounter18 must raise an illegal‑instruction exception. The value read from hpmcounter18 always reflects the current value of mhpmcounter18 and continues to increment independently of the enable bits.
